{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman / Sparkling)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Subject:** Playbook review findings, redline status and negotiation priorities

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Software License and Maintenance Agreement against the playbook and recorded 18 findings: 10 compliant, 6 deviations and 2 missing clauses. The commercial architecture is broadly favourable to us — the licence is perpetual so long as fees are paid, we hold an unqualified termination-for-convenience right on 90 days' notice, the Vendor's IP indemnity is uncapped, the Section 12 warranty exceeds our preferred 12-month position, and there is no exclusivity, non-compete, minimum commitment, MFN, auto-renewal, liquidated damages or vendor audit right anywhere in the document.

Four issues drive the negotiation. First, Section 20(d) imposes an absolute consent requirement on assignment with no affiliate or M&A carve-out, reinforced by Section 3(c) and by the "non-transferable" licence grant in Section 2 — we cannot move this contract to a successor. Second, Section 15 contains no monetary cap at all, so both parties bear unlimited direct-damages exposure, failing the fallback's 12-month-fees floor. Third, the Agreement is silent on Vendor insurance even though Garman installs software at our sites and converts our data. Fourth, there is no post-termination transition assistance or data return and deletion obligation on Garman. Governing law (Nova Scotia), the ownership sweep in Section 13 and the Section 19 no-hire round out the deviations.

Three of our proposed redlines did not pass verification (Licence grant scope, Transition assistance, Non-solicitation) and require manual drafting before the markup goes out. Three others were auto-repaired and should be read closely on the final pass.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant (fallback) | Page 6 (§ 13) | Uncapped Vendor IP indemnity, better than the fallback super-cap; no express duty to defend, no refund remedy, 10-day notice window — noted only. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License | No exclusivity, sole-supplier or minimum-requirements obligation; licence and escrow licence are non-exclusive. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No liquidated damages, penalty, late interest or exit fee; § 17 runs in our favour. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | Ordinary licence use restrictions only; § 19 is a mutual non-solicit, not a non-compete. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (fallback) | § 17 Term and Termination | § 17(b) gives us convenience termination on 90 days' notice, no exit fee; Vendor has no convenience right. No express pro-rata refund — noted. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant (better than preferred) | § 3 Restrictions on Use | No Vendor audit or usage-verification right; only inspection right (§ 16 escrow) runs in our favour. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | Page 10 (§ 20(h)) | Nova Scotia law and courts fall outside the accepted list; venue is non-exclusive, which mitigates. Proposal: New York law, exclusive New York County courts. |
| Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 Grant of License | Perpetual and covers affiliates, but "non-transferable" with §§ 3(c)/20(d) consent gates leaves no successor path; contractors excluded. **Redline verification failed — manual drafting required.** |
| Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No MFN in either direction; an MFN in our favour is a commercial ask, not required by the rule. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume | Compliant | § 11 Fees | Fees payable for licence and services actually taken; maintenance is a renewable one-year term. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant (better than fallback) | § 10 Maintenance and Support | No evergreen renewal; renewal by election. No CPI/3% uplift cap, but no unilateral uplift right either — noted. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | Page 9 (§ 17) | No Vendor obligation to assist on exit, return our data or certify deletion; § 8(b) applies only on § 7 rejection. **Redline verification failed — manual drafting required.** |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant (exceeds preferred) | § 12 Specifications and Warranty | Warranty for acceptance period plus one year and for the life of Maintenance Services; no "AS IS" or implied-warranty disclaimer. No services/malicious-code warranty — noted. |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation (walk-away)** | Page 10 (§ 20(d)) | Blanket consent requirement, no affiliate or M&A carve-out, no reasonableness standard. Auto-repaired redline adds carve-out, reasonableness, competitor bar and change-of-control confirmation. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing (walk-away)** | Page 10 (§ 20) | No insurance covenant anywhere, yet Garman installs on-site and converts our data. Auto-repaired redline inserts preferred-position § 20(j); fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |
| Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Garman ownership sweeps in "all related materials, logos, and names" and the funded Schedule "D" Modifications; no statement that we retain rights in our data. Auto-repaired redline narrows ownership, adds data ownership and a perpetual licence to funded Modifications. |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability | No monetary cap at all, so unlimited direct-damages exposure for us; fails the 12-month-fees fallback. Auto-repaired redline inserts mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000) with uncapped carve-outs. |
| Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees | Drafted as a no-hire covering all employees of the other party, with no advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-outs. **Redline verification failed — manual drafting required.** |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **Assignment — § 20(d) (with § 3(c)):** a blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out. We need, at minimum, the fallback: a mutual right to assign to a successor on written notice, with consent otherwise not unreasonably withheld.
2. **Vendor insurance — § 20 (absent):** a vendor that works on our premises and processes our data carries no insurance obligation at all. Preferred position inserted as new § 20(j); E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is the acceptable fallback.
3. **Non-solicitation — § 19:** a no-hire covering all of the other party's employees. We need conversion to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.

We also treat the absence of any liability cap in § 15 as a priority ask, since the unlimited exposure runs against us as well as Garman.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Manual drafting (before markup issues):** prepare redlines for LICENSE (§ 2 — contractors and successor transfer), TRANSITION (new § 17 exit assistance, machine-readable data return within 30 days, deletion certification; 90 days' assistance is an acceptable fallback) and NOSOLICIT (§ 19 rewrite). The automated proposals for these three did not verify.
2. **Quality-check the auto-repaired redlines** for ASSIGN, INSURANCE, IP and LOL-CAP against the section text before circulation.
3. **Send the markup with the four priority asks front-loaded:** assignment carve-out, § 15 mutual cap, § 20(j) insurance, § 19 non-solicit; then governing law (New York, exclusive New York County courts), the § 13 ownership narrowing and the § 2 transfer right.
4. **Raise conversationally, not by redline:** express duty to defend and a longer indemnity notice window (§ 13); 30 days' notice and an express pro-rata refund on convenience termination (§ 17(b)); a CPI/3% cap on renewal maintenance fees if the Fee Schedule is reopened; a services, malicious-code and compliance-with-laws warranty (§ 12); and, as a commercial ask only, an MFN in our favour.
5. **Hold the line on current advantages:** resist any Vendor attempt to introduce an audit or usage-verification right (and if one is introduced, insist on once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, vendor cost, no system access), and preserve the mutual exclusion of consequential damages and the § 13/§ 14 carve-outs as drafted.
6. **Escalate to the business** if Garman refuses any of the three walk-away items, so that the sponsor can weigh signature risk before we trade elsewhere."}
